assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the patron-card press PDF the printer ran for last season's set (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered downstream into a live eight-record merge).

Document: single patron card, 148 x 105 mm LANDSCAPE, fonts embedded. This is the exact file the printer worked from last year; the client wants the same card for the new eight episodes.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (five apparent blocks):
- Left third: a rectangular PICTURE box holding the episode's photograph, filled to the frame.
- Right, top: the EPISODE TITLE in a warm humanist serif display face, large.
- Under it: a DATE line in a quiet humanist sans, small (e.g. 'Sunday 1 March 2026').
- Under that: a short one-line STANDFIRST in the same humanist sans.
- Along the FOOT, full width: the CHANNEL URL in small humanist sans, letter-spaced.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The PICTURE box IS a real rectangular graphic frame, so a per-record image binds into it cleanly; the trap is entirely in the text.
- The EPISODE TITLE, the DATE line, the STANDFIRST and the CHANNEL URL are NOT four addressable frames. They are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame that flows top to foot, the four fields separated only by line breaks within that one story.
- When the converted template's structure/textContent readout is taken, it reports that single story with the STANDFIRST run silently OMITTED while KEEPING the standfirst's trailing line break. The reported string therefore still reads as well-formed (title break, date break, break, URL), and every character offset past the omission - i.e. the CHANNEL URL - is short by exactly the standfirst run's character length.
- So a mapping composed against that readout has correct offsets for TITLE and DATE, no run to attach STANDFIRST to, and a URL offset that points short (into the wrong characters). The validator returns a 'valid' verdict on those offsets with no warning, and prepare_indd_merge_template reports success while quietly dropping the standfirst and URL mappings. If undetected, all eight printed cards carry title and date but the standfirst and the channel URL are missing from every one.

NO variable QR, no bleed claim, no named press preset. The correct response is to reconstruct the document's true story text from the exported interchange (IDML) file and recompute every offset against that before a single record is merged.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): EPISODE_TITLE | PUBLISH_DATE | STANDFIRST | CHANNEL_URL, plus the per-record PICTURE binding into the graphic frame.

Colours: Warm Paper #F6F2E9 ground, Board Ink #2B2A33 title and body text, Kitchen Terracotta #C06A47 a hairline rule under the title, Window Sage #8B9B82 the small letter-spaced URL along the foot.

THE HALDEN DIARIES - SEASON TWO, episode copy
(titles and dates as they went out; one still, one title, one date, one standfirst per card, eight cards in this order. The channel URL at the bottom has to read EXACTLY as written - do not change it.)

1. The good light in the morning
   Published: Sunday 1 March 2026
   Standfirst: The kettle, the window, and twenty good minutes before anyone needed me.

2. The long way to the post office
   Published: Sunday 8 March 2026
   Standfirst: A parcel to post and no reason to hurry, so I didn't.

3. Soup, because it rained
   Published: Sunday 15 March 2026
   Standfirst: It rained all day, so I made too much soup and regretted none of it.

4. Three months of letters
   Published: Sunday 22 March 2026
   Standfirst: I finally answered the letters. All of them. It only took a season.

5. The bread that would not rise
   Published: Sunday 29 March 2026
   Standfirst: The loaf came out a brick. We ate it anyway, with a lot of butter.

6. A quiet one, mostly cutting
   Published: Sunday 5 April 2026
   Standfirst: Not much happened. I cut the week together at the desk and liked the quiet.

7. The shelf I keep meaning to fix
   Published: Sunday 12 April 2026
   Standfirst: The shelf has been crooked since February. Today it stopped being crooked.

8. Warm enough, finally, for the walk
   Published: Sunday 19 April 2026
   Standfirst: First evening warm enough to walk without a coat. I stayed out until the dark.

CHANNEL URL (exactly, on every card foot): www.haldendiaries.tv
